rows.selection_reason: The existing evidence is empty, so the first experiment should test a multimodal setup with strong encoders (scgpt and imagenet_vit_l) and complex aggregation/fusion (transformer + weighted) to evaluate if multimodal approaches outperform single-modality baselines. This configuration isolates key design choices (encoders, aggregation, fusion) critical for performance, balancing exploration of multimodal potential while using high-quality components.

Existing evidence shows that config_001 (multimodal, multiprofile, scgpt, imagenet_vit_l, transformer, weighted) achieves moderate performance. This experiment tests replacing the image encoder with resnet50 and switching fusion from weighted to concat, isolating the impact of these two design choices. It directly compares aggregation/fusion strategies and image encoder variants while keeping RNA encoder and profile settings consistent, providing critical insights with minimal parameter changes.

Existing evidence shows config_001 (weighted fusion, 0.52 accuracy) outperforms config_022 (concat fusion, 0.47 accuracy), but config_022 uses resnet50 instead of imagenet_vit_l. This experiment tests whether changing fusion from weighted to concat while keeping RNA/image encoders and aggregation the same (as in config_001) affects performance, isolating the fusion method's impact. It is the best next step as it directly addresses a key design choice with minimal parameter changes.

Existing evidence shows that config_001 (transformer aggregation, weighted fusion) has the highest accuracy. This experiment tests whether switching to avgpool aggregation (while keeping scgpt RNA, imagenet_vit_l image, and weighted fusion) improves performance, isolating the impact of aggregation method. This clarifies whether transformer is critical or if avgpool could be a simpler alternative, balancing exploration and exploitation.

Existing evidence shows config_038 (avgpool aggregation, weighted fusion) achieves the highest validation accuracy (0.542). This experiment tests changing the RNA encoder from scgpt to scvi_n200 while keeping image encoder, aggregation, and fusion methods identical, isolating the effect of the RNA encoder choice. This directly addresses whether the RNA representation significantly impacts performance, building on the strong baseline of config_038.

The existing evidence shows that config_046 (scvi_n200 RNA, ViT image, avgpool, weighted) achieves the highest accuracy. This experiment tests whether replacing ViT with ResNet50 image encoder (while keeping avgpool and weighted fusion) affects performance, isolating the impact of the image encoder choice. This is critical for determining if ViT's superiority is consistent or if ResNet50 could be a viable alternative under different conditions.

Existing evidence shows that scvi_n200 RNA encoder and imagenet_vit_l image encoder combinations (config_046, config_029) achieve high accuracy. This experiment tests whether changing aggregation from avgpool (used in config_046) to transformer (used in config_042) improves performance, isolating the effect of aggregation method. It balances exploitation of promising components (scvi_n200/imagenet_vit_l) with exploration of a key design choice (aggregation).

Existing evidence shows that using transformer aggregation with weighted fusion (config_042, 0.725 accuracy) outperforms avgpool with weighted fusion (config_046, 0.706). This experiment tests whether switching to concat fusion while keeping transformer aggregation and other parameters (scvi_n200 RNA, imagenet_vit_l image, multiprofile) the same isolates the impact of fusion method. It directly addresses uncertainty about whether weighted vs concat fusion is critical, leveraging the strong prior evidence for scvi_n200 and imagenet_vit_l.

Existing evidence shows that using scvi_n200 RNA encoder, transformer aggregation, and weighted fusion achieves high performance (config_042: 0.725 accuracy). This experiment tests whether switching the image encoder from imagenet_vit_l (used in config_042) to resnet50 (a simpler model) affects performance, isolating the impact of the image encoder choice. It balances exploitation of the scvi_n200 RNA encoder and transformer aggregation while exploring a key design decision (image encoder) that may influence performance.

Existing evidence shows that scvi_n200 RNA encoder and imagenet_vit_l image encoder with transformer aggregation and weighted fusion achieve top performance. This experiment tests using resnet50 image encoder with pca_n2000 RNA encoder, transformer aggregation, and weighted fusion to isolate the impact of image encoder and RNA encoder choices. It clarifies whether resnet50 (vs imagenet_vit_l) or pca_n2000 (vs scvi_n200) affects performance, while maintaining transformer aggregation and weighted fusion, which are already shown to be effective.
